title: THE SERVANT OF THE LORD DIES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua dismissed the people, each to their own inheritance. After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of a hundred and ten. And they buried him in the land of his inheritance, at Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash. — Josh 24:28-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The great leader's story comes to a close. Joshua dies at a hundred and ten, and Scripture gives him a title that says everything: "the servant of the Lord." Not "the great conqueror" or "the mighty general," though he was both. His truest honor was that he served the Lord.

Think of all Joshua had seen — the crossing of the Jordan, the fall of Jericho, the sun standing still, the whole land settled. Yet at the end, what mattered was not his achievements but his faithfulness. He served God, and he finished well. He was buried in his own inheritance, in the land God had promised, having done what God gave him to do.

This is the title worth having. The world hands out many honors, but there is none greater than to be called a servant of the Lord. Jesus taught that the way to greatness in His kingdom is through servanthood (Mark 10:43-44), and He Himself came not to be served but to serve.

One day our own story will close, as Joshua's did. What title will fit our lives? Not our positions or possessions, but our faithfulness to God, will be what remains. Live so that "servant of the Lord" would be a fitting summary of your days. Serve Him faithfully now, and by His grace, finish well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Would "servant of the Lord" describe your life?
2. Why is faithfulness more important than achievement in God's eyes?
3. What would it mean for you to finish well in your walk with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, more than any earthly honor, I want to be found Your faithful servant. Help me to serve You wholeheartedly and, by Your grace, to finish well. Amen.
